title: Hello, Dinosaurs!

pages.title: Hello, Dinosaurs!
pages.caption: Twelve prehistoric animals to meet.
pages.speech: Hello, dinosaur explorers! Let us meet twelve amazing prehistoric animals. Tap a picture to hear its name. The sound button plays an imagined animal call.

pages.title: Tyrannosaurus rex
pages.caption: Two strong legs and tiny arms.
pages.speech: Tyrannosaurus rex walked on two strong legs. Its arms were small. Can you find them?

pages.title: Triceratops
pages.caption: Three horns. One, two, three!
pages.speech: Triceratops had three horns and a wide frill. Can you count the horns? One, two, three!

pages.title: Stegosaurus
pages.caption: Tall plates along its back.
pages.speech: Stegosaurus had tall plates along its back and spikes on its tail. Point to a plate, then a spike.

pages.title: Brachiosaurus
pages.caption: Front legs longer than back legs.
pages.speech: Brachiosaurus had a long neck. Its front legs were longer than its back legs. Imagine reaching high into a leafy tree.

pages.title: Diplodocus
pages.caption: A very long, slender tail.
pages.speech: Diplodocus had a long neck and a very long, slender tail. Follow the tail with your finger. Where does it end?

pages.title: Ankylosaurus
pages.caption: Armour and a tail club.
pages.speech: Ankylosaurus wore bony armour. Its tail ended in a heavy club. Can you spot the club in the picture?

pages.title: Brontosaurus
pages.caption: A long neck and sturdy legs.
pages.speech: Brontosaurus was a giant plant eater with a long neck and sturdy legs. Imagine its slow steps through the ferns.

pages.title: Spinosaurus
pages.caption: A tall sail and a long snout.
pages.speech: Spinosaurus had a tall sail on its back and a long snout. It ate fish. Can you trace the shape of its sail?

pages.title: Pteranodon
pages.caption: A flying reptile, not a dinosaur.
pages.speech: Pteranodon was a flying reptile, not a dinosaur. It had a long beak and wide wings. Spread your arms like wings!

pages.title: Quetzalcoatlus
pages.caption: Another amazing flying reptile.
pages.speech: Quetzalcoatlus was another flying reptile. It had a long neck and an enormous wingspan. Imagine the shadow of those wings.

pages.title: Parasaurolophus
pages.caption: A curved crest on its head.
pages.speech: Parasaurolophus had a long curved crest on its head. Scientists think its crest may have helped it make sounds. What do you imagine?

pages.title: Velociraptor
pages.caption: A small dinosaur with feathers.
pages.speech: Velociraptor was much smaller than the giants in this book. It had feathers. Look for the feathers on its arms and tail.

pages.title: Who will you choose?
pages.caption: Tap an animal to hear its name again.
pages.speech: Which animal would you like to meet again? Some lived millions of years apart. Their real voices are a mystery, so our sounds are made for imagination.

notes: Original text. Illustrative colours and imaginative calls; no claim animals coexisted. Pterosaurs are flying reptiles.
